title: Security lab: triage a file
intro: This walk-through makes a harmless script that looks like a dropper, then examines it the way you'd examine a real sample. To work on your own file, use Upload (or drop it on the terminal); it lands in /root/uploads.

steps.text: Create the sample. It only prints text, but hides it in base64 the way droppers do.
steps.cmd:
mkdir -p ~/lab && cd ~/lab && printf '#!/bin/sh
# installer
U=http://example.invalid/payload
echo ZWNobyAidGhpcyBpcyBvbmx5IGEgdGVzdCI= | base64 -d | sh
' > sample.sh

steps.text: Never trust the name. Ask what the file really is.
Record its fingerprint so you can look it up and refer to it later.
Pull out readable text: URLs, commands, paths.
Decode the hidden part without running it.
Write a YARA rule for this pattern: download URL plus a base64-to-shell pipe.
steps.cmd:
printf 'rule b64_pipe_to_shell {
  strings:
    $url = "http://"
    $pipe = /base64 -d \| *sh/
  condition:
    $url and $pipe
}
' > dropper.yar && cat dropper.yar

steps.text: Now run it, watching every system call it makes. It's safe: it only echoes.
Uploaded a binary? Check its type, then its headers. Windows files work with pefile; ELF with readelf.
